newsitem.title: HUNGARY: WHEAT STEALS SHOW ON HECTIC BUDAPEST GRAINS MKT.
newsitem.headline: WHEAT STEALS SHOW ON HECTIC BUDAPEST GRAINS MKT.

text.p: Milling wheat futures attracted the most deals the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) but the market was still looking for a suitable price range, traders said on Thursday.
"It will take two to three weeks to asses the damage bad weather has caused to crops and to have appropriate estimates," said Robert Vajo of Termin.
Milling wheat prices moved in opposite directions as May, August, October and December finished lower while July and March rose.
Milling wheat futures accounted for 2,128 contracts out of a total grains turnover of 2,265 contracts or 1.13 billion forints.
Maize remained almost untraded with only 25 July contracts and 95 December contracts changing hands and Vajo said that was due to lack of buyers.
"There were producers willing to sell, but after Wednesday's fairly significant turnover buyers have retreated," he said.
July maize went down by the daily 400-forint limit to 19,500 forints whle the other traded month, December reimaned steady.
